subject: POC: Prompt set & eval plan for Acme Health - next steps
messages:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC recap + prompt/eval plan (Acme Health)

Thanks again for the call this morning, Alex - great alignment on the trial scope. Per our discussion, here's a concise recap and proposed next steps for the POC focused on the clinical triage assistant use case:

Summary of goals:
- Verify response accuracy on clinician-facing triage prompts (reduce hallucination rate)
- Meet latency SLOs under concurrent load (95th perc < 300ms for short prompts)
- Validate retrieval/soft prompt pipeline with de-identified logs

Proposed success criteria (we can refine):
- Precision on medication extraction >= 92% on our labeled eval set
- Hallucination rate <= 4% measured by reviewer tags
- Average token cost reduction plan by >= 20% using batching/caching

Evaluation plan / deliverables:
1) Customer provides prompt set + representative logs (CSV) and an initial labeled eval subset (~500 prompts) - see template attached.
2) Redwood to run baseline model configs and share per-prompt metrics (accuracy, helpfulness, hallucination flag).
3) Joint review session week-of Mar 30 to review results and tune prompts/metrics.

Ownership:
- Customer: provide prompt set, de-identified logs, and a small labeled eval subset (Alex / Samantha)
- Redwood: run evals, share metrics, provide optimization suggestions (Marissa lead; Rishi SE will own test harness)

Timeline (proposed):
- Mar 23: Customer shares the prompt CSV + any security constraints
- Mar 25-27: Redwood runs initial evals and returns draft report
- Mar 30: Joint results review and go/no-go decision for expanded pilot

Attachments: acmehealth_poc_prompts_v1.csv (prompt template), acme_security_questionnaire.pdf

Next step for you: please confirm you can share the CSV by EOD Mon (Mar 23). If there are any restrictions on logs (PHI, retention), flag them in your reply.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC recap + prompt/eval plan (Acme Health)

Thanks Alex - and great, appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple technical Qs to make sure we can run the evals smoothly:

1) CSV format: will each row be one prompt + expected label(s)? If you can follow the attached template (prompt, context, expected_label, label_confidence), that helps our harness.
2) Logs: can you indicate whether timestamps are UTC and if records include session IDs? Session IDs let us simulate realistic conversation threading for caching tests.
3) Redaction: please confirm PHI fields are removed or masked and include a note in the cover email about which fields were scrubbed. That will speed security review.

On our side, we'll provision a test harness that produces per-prompt metrics: exact match, partial match, hallucination_flag, generation_time_ms, token_usage. We'll share a sample CSV of our metrics output so you can map fields to your internal trackers.

I'll own the eval run. Marissa - please confirm whether you'd like the baseline to include a quantized Llama-2-70B variant or stick to the open Llama-2-13B for first pass (tradeoff: 70B may improve accuracy but will increase cost/latency).

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: eval_output_template.csv - stub)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC recap + prompt/eval plan (Acme Health)

Thanks Rishi - answers below:

- CSV format: yes, one prompt per row with expected_label. We'll use the template you attached.
- Timestamps: UTC, yes. We can include session IDs for a subset (about 25% of rows) to help with caching simulations.
- Redaction: PHI is removed; we'll include a short data-handling note in the cover email describing the scrub steps.

On model choice: start with Llama-2-13B for baseline. If we need better extraction accuracy, we'll explore 70B for a second run. Cost sensitivity is real for us, so showing the tradeoffs will be useful.

Also confirming our initial labeled eval subset will be ~500 prompts, as discussed. We expect to drop the files in the Drive folder you shared.

-Alex
